the following: (i) the evaluation of the energy performance and thermal comfort in an existing office building after its transformation into a nearly zero-energy building; (ii) the evaluation of visual comfort in the same building; (iii) the assessment of the implications on the energy performance and visual comfort after the transformation of the building.

the nZEB refurbishment of existing office buildings is possible with the achievement of both energy savings and thermal comfort, but it would lead to a reduction in daylighting and a consequent increase in electricity demand for lighting.
a nZEB retrofit scenario, with the proposed measures, would not be a suitable solution for an office building.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the energy retrofit actions on building envelope and lighting would lead to a reduction of the energy demand and to an improvement of the indoor thermal environment, but a reduction of the visual comfort would occur.
the nZEB concept should be applied in an integrated way to ensure the best trade-off in terms of energy savings, thermal comfort and lighting quality.
the envelope retrofit is not the only solution to reach the nearly zero energy building target.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retrofitting of existing office buildings to nZEB should not only focus on energy efficiency, but also on the thermal and visual comfort.
a holistic approach should be adopted to assess the energy performance of buildings, including the thermal, visual, and energy aspects.
